title: Partitioning and the hot key problem

claims.text: The 2007 system partitions and replicates data using consistent hashing, which is chosen so that the arrival or departure of a node redistributes only the keys adjacent to it rather than remapping the whole space. The design is completely decentralised with minimal need for manual administration, and uses a gossip-based protocol for membership and failure detection.

source.title: Giuseppe DeCandia, Deniz Hastorun, Madan Jampani, Gunavardhan Kakulapati, Avinash Lakshman, Alex Pilchin, Swaminathan Sivasubramanian, Peter Vosshall and Werner Vogels, Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store, Proceedings of the 21st ACM Symposium on Operating Systems Principles, 2007, pages 205-220, doi 10.1145/1294261.1294281

claims.text: The interface constraint that follows from partitioning is stated plainly: the system has no isolation and allows only single-key updates. Operations that would span partitions are not offered rather than being offered slowly.

source.title: Giuseppe DeCandia, Deniz Hastorun, Madan Jampani, Gunavardhan Kakulapati, Avinash Lakshman, Alex Pilchin, Swaminathan Sivasubramanian, Peter Vosshall and Werner Vogels, Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store, Proceedings of the 21st ACM Symposium on Operating Systems Principles, 2007, pages 205-220, doi 10.1145/1294261.1294281

beats.broke: the data no longer fits on one machine, or the writes to it no longer fit, and replication does not help because every copy still holds everything
beats.fix: split the data by a key so each machine holds a disjoint share, choosing the mapping so that adding or removing a machine moves as little as possible rather than remapping everything
beats.cost: the split is only as even as the key's distribution, so a single popular value concentrates load on one partition regardless of how many machines exist — and operations spanning partitions become expensive or simply unavailable
beats.interview: what happens when one key is far more popular than the others
